title: Ken Shoulders' ceramic puncture experiment
summary: Dave Rossi tells of Ken Shoulders' ceramic puncture experiment, about undated at unspecified, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: Ken Shoulders had an experiment, and please correct me if I'm wrong, where basically he found that electrical pulses into a ceramic would break not break ceramic, but create these punctures in the ceramic that electricity normally wouldn't do.

plain: A guest named Dave Rossi, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, describes an experiment by an electrical researcher named Ken Shoulders. Rossi says Shoulders found that sending electrical pulses into a piece of ceramic did not break it but made small punctures through it, something ordinary electricity should not do. He tells it as a hint, if true, of unusual physics that conventional science has overlooked.
